ideas.title: Glass hour
ideas.critique: It has the same shape as the grey-draft patch: a zone sweeps over the island and changes how everything looks, then goes away. What is strong is the payoff only a path tracer can give, coloured caustics through glass friends in mid-step. But it rests entirely on the light being right, and a plain glass swap with weak caustics would read as a filter.

ideas.title: The sky is a mirror
ideas.critique: Turning the sky itself into a curved conductor changes what the world is, and no raster engine would show it. The only echo is the TV's self-image. The risk is that a dome reflection of a small island mostly shows sea and blur, so the upside-down friends have to be readable or the idea is lost.

ideas.title: Day and night share the island
ideas.critique: A drifting boundary that changes the friends' state as it passes them is the zone-plus-reaction recipe of Slow time and the grey patch. Two skies split on one island is a real lighting stunt. The yawning and waking gag is predictable.

ideas.title: Lumi wakes up in Gloop
ideas.critique: Nothing on the island has swapped Lumi's own body and gait, and the friends' confusion about who to talk to is a fresh social beat. Still, body-swap comedy is a familiar trope, and made as a clumsy-minutes gag film it lands close to the spoken-gag set-pieces.

ideas.title: The sea keeps a second island
ideas.critique: Copies of the friends acting in counterpoint are Yesterday's ghosts plus the live mirror island out at sea, with moods flipped. This is one more mirror-copy place. The traced glassy sea is the only new part.

ideas.title: Voices print on the waves
ideas.critique: Speech leaving a lasting physical trace in the world is exactly what the last three sand posts did, with water swapped for dunes. Scalograms as signatures is clever, but to a viewer it will look like glowing stripes on the sea after the sand run.

ideas.title: Bronze keepsakes
ideas.nearest: Me, to cut out and fold
ideas.critique: A tool that turns a creature into a small physical copy placed somewhere is the papercraft-Lumi move again. Freezing real poses in worn metal is a good materials showcase, and the shelf filling up over time has charm. It is one more permanent prop, so it is capped low.

ideas.title: Through the island
ideas.critique: A creature reshaping the ground, then a ride down it, continues the terrain-gag streak that just ran four posts. Coming out of the sea upside down on the far side is a good punchline. The dig itself is slow and invisible for most of its length.

ideas.title: Lumi's own moon
ideas.critique: A moving light the friends chase is the moth again with a cannon added. A searchlight sweeping the island at night is pleasant but expected for a lighting goal, so this is one more prop plus chase behaviour.

ideas.title: The island in a medal
ideas.critique: It is again a whole-island transform event that comes and goes, like the seesaw and the draft patch. Friends moving as raised outlines across a bronze relief is a strong, odd image that changes what the island is for a minute. It only works if the relief actually moves, not if it is a static flattened mesh.
